sources.author: Shreya Kapoor
sources.headline: Staff Engineer @ Anthropic | Building agent infrastructure | Ex-Google
sources.post_summary: Posted about how Claude Code's new persistent memory across sessions is changing their internal dev workflows — engineers are spending 40% less time re-explaining context to AI. Included a short demo of a multi-session bug fix that required zero re-prompting. Sparked debate in comments about whether AI memory is a feature or a crutch.

sources.author: Marcus Delgado
sources.headline: Founder @ Argo AI Infra | ex-AWS | Helping teams cut LLM costs by 60%
sources.post_summary: Shared a teardown of a $140k/month LLM bill that got reduced to $52k in 30 days without changing model quality — the culprit was unoptimized context windows and redundant embedding calls. Called out the pattern of 'inference bloat' as the new cloud waste. Post hit because it had a real before/after architecture diagram.

sources.author: Priya Nambiar
sources.headline: Head of Product @ Vertex | AI Automation | GTM Engineering
sources.post_summary: Wrote about deploying a multi-agent system that replaced a 6-person SDR team — not to fire people, but to redeploy them into higher-leverage roles. Framed it as the first real case of 'AI expansion, not replacement' she'd seen work at scale. Comments are split between skeptics asking for the data and practitioners sharing similar stories.

sources.author: Tom Okafor
sources.headline: DevTools Investor @ Gradient | Prev: Vercel, Linear | Open source advocate
sources.post_summary: Called MCP (Model Context Protocol) the 'USB-C moment for AI tooling' — argued that within 18 months, any dev tool without an MCP server will feel as outdated as software without an API. Listed 12 tools that shipped MCP servers this week alone. The comment section became an unofficial MCP directory.

sources.author: Kyle Coleman
sources.headline: CMO at Clari | Revenue Intelligence | GTM Advisor
sources.post_summary: Most outbound teams are running 2019 playbooks in 2026. The reps sending 500 generic emails/day are getting 0.1% reply rates while the teams running 50 hyper-personalized sequences with buying signal triggers are hitting 8-12%. The volume era is over. Signal-led outbound is the only motion that still works.

sources.author: Maggie Zhu
sources.headline: RevOps Lead @ Series B SaaS | GTM Systems | Clay + HubSpot
sources.post_summary: We cut our SDR team from 8 to 3 and doubled pipeline in 6 months. Not by working harder — by rebuilding the entire GTM stack around Clay, Apollo, and one AI sequencing layer. The 3 remaining SDRs now do what 8 couldn't: they only touch accounts that have shown 3+ buying signals in the last 30 days.

sources.author: Jason Vargas
sources.headline: Head of Sales Development @ Rippling | Outbound Obsessed
sources.post_summary: Hot take: your content strategy IS your outbound strategy now. Buyers ignore cold email but they're reading your LinkedIn posts. The reps who comment thoughtfully on ICP content and post their own POVs are booking 3x more meetings than reps who just dial and blast. Social proximity beats cold reach every time.

sources.author: Priya Nath
sources.headline: GTM Engineer | Building revenue systems at the intersection of AI + ops | ex-Salesforce
sources.post_summary: The GTM Engineer role didn't exist 3 years ago. Now it's the most important hire in a sub-50 person GTM org. Not a salesperson. Not a marketer. Not a traditional ops hire. Someone who can write a Clay enrichment waterfall, prompt Claude to score ICPs, and push a HubSpot workflow — all before lunch. This is what modern revenue infrastructure looks like.

sources.author: Marcus Chen
sources.headline: Indie hacker | Shipped 6 products in 12 months | $47K MRR | Building in public
sources.post_summary: Crossed $47K MRR yesterday with zero VC funding. 18 months ago I was a burned-out senior engineer at a FAANG. The turning point wasn't a viral post or a lucky break — it was shipping something ugly every 2 weeks until one stuck. Here's the exact timeline.

sources.author: Priya Nair
sources.headline: Ex-nurse turned developer | Shipped my first SaaS in 90 days | Healthcare AI
sources.post_summary: I learned to code while working 12-hour hospital shifts. No bootcamp. No CS degree. Just YouTube, Claude, and a problem I lived every day. My app for nurse scheduling just hit 200 paying users. Every 'you're not technical enough' DM was fuel.

sources.author: Jordan Okafor
sources.headline: Solo dev building vertical AI agents | 3 products live | ex-Shopify
sources.post_summary: I replaced my entire market research workflow with a Claude agent I built in a weekend. What used to take 6 hours now takes 11 minutes. I'm open-sourcing the architecture today — link in comments. This is what 'AI-native' actually means in practice.

sources.author: Sofia Reyes
sources.headline: Product designer → founder | Building B2B tools for small teams | Revenue-first
sources.post_summary: Week 14 of building in public. Honest numbers: $2,100 MRR, 3 churned customers, 1 enterprise lead that went cold. Most build-in-public posts show the wins. I'm showing the loss review I ran last Sunday and what it changed about our ICP.
